messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] sflist2stanfit help minor error
parts:
[moved to stan-dev]

Is it hard to fix the output so it doesn't say "Error"
when there's not an error? Every time we say error, it
confuses our users. Even if we say "warning (this is NOT an error)"
it confuses our users.

I understand's CRAN has issues with anything that takes longer
than a few seconds or consumes more than a few megabytes of memory.
For what it's worth, compilation is about 15s for a very simple model
on my Macbook Pro using clang++ -O3 in RStan 2.6. I believe g++
is much slower.

- Bob

> On Feb 26, 2015, at 12:27 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

> There is a suggestion by CRAN that examples take 5 seconds or less, which is about 1 / 5 of the time we need to compile a model. I agree that it would be better if the word "Error" did not appear but the documentation does say that the stanfit object is created even if there are runtime errors. If you instead source and use
>
> http://mc-stan.org/rstan/stan.R
>
> it suppresses that particular message.
>
> Ben
